title: Ephemeral admission proxy replication and backpressure heuristics for cross-region SLO retention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our current global admission path uses a centralized credit manager per region. During partial outages or planned maintenance the credit manager can become unreachable for seconds-to-minutes which causes either hard rejects or uncoordinated retries that spike downstream latency and burn SLOs.

Goal: Introduce an ephemeral admission proxy that maintains soft-state replica of recent credit allocations and a conservative backpressure heuristic (hedged credits + staged admission) to allow local, safe admissions during short credit-controller blackouts and to replay accumulated soft-credits when the controller returns. The feature must preserve p95/p99 latency SLOs for latency-sensitive hosts, minimize cross-region unfairness, and not allow credit double-spend across nodes.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace global quota reconciliation or long-term accounting; it only addresses short-lived (<= 2 minutes) admission-controller unavailability and graceful recovery. Full offline reconciliation strategy handled in follow-up.

Acceptance criteria: 
- During controller blackout simulations (up to 120s) traffic continues to be admitted using ephemeral soft-credits with <3% increase in tail latency and <10% additional error budget burn across impacted tenants.
- No observed double-counting of committed credits in 1000-run randomized test harness.
- When controller returns we perform deterministic replay/reconciliation with bounded retraction window and emit audit events to console and billing pipeline.
- Metrics and dashboards for ephemeral-proxy hit-rate, replay volume, conservative-admit-rate, and reconciliation failures are added to the Console with per-tenant filters.

Design summary: 
- Ephemeral admission proxy runs co-located with the tenant-facing gateway in each AZ. It maintains an append-only recent-credit log and a lightweight lease with the region's credit-controller.
- On normal operation it forwards admissions to region controller; it continuously pulls deltas to keep soft-state warm.
- On controller heartbeat loss, proxy switches to local conservative admit policy: allow up to median-request-size * hedged_factor tokens per tenant per second from the soft-state cache and charge them as "speculative".
- The proxy marks speculative admissions in audit logs; once controller is reachable, the proxy performs batched deterministic reconciliation and either commits speculative charges or issues compensating retractions (rate-limited).
- To avoid double-spend we use monotonic per-tenant sequence tokens and idempotent admission receipts.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive local admission reduces user-facing errors but risks overspend; we cap hedged_factor and prioritize latency-sensitive API keys.
- Stronger correctness (e.g., synchronous quorum writes) would add cross-region latency; we opted for local fast-path plus deterministic reconciliation to preserve SLOs.

Telemetry & rollback: 
- Add feature flags and per-tenant opt-in so we can gate for enterprise customers during initial rollout.
- Dashboards: speculative_admit_rate, speculative_commit_rate, reconciliation_rejections, speculative_cost_estimate, and controller_heartbeat_lag.
- Automatic rollback if reconciliation_rejections > 0.5% for two consecutive 10m windows.

Operational runbook excerpt: 
- If speculative_commit_rate spike with high reconciliation_rejections, flip feature flag for affected region and open incident runbook 'admission-proxy-reconcile'.
- During planned controller upgrades enable read-only warm-sync mode rather than speculative admit (controlled via release toggle).

Implement hedged credit admission policy and per-tenant sequencing
Integrate idempotent receipts in controller and gateway; add reconciliation API endpoints
Build simulation harness for blackout scenarios (unit + chaos tests)
Expose telemetry and console dashboards; add alert thresholds
Canary rollout: 1% tenants in us-west-2, monitor 72h, then 10%
Documentation: runbook, SDK behavioral notes, billing implications
comments: 2026-01-18 - Asha Patel: RFC posted to Confluence. Initial microbenchmarks show local soft-state lookups add <1ms to median admission path. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ephemeral-admission-proxy

2026-01-22 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented prototype sidecar; pushed branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1832. Early integration tests pass but reconciliation retries need rate limiting to avoid thundering herd.

2026-01-25 - Priya Rao (SRE reviewer): Reviewed design. Requested stronger invariants around sequence tokens and auditability; recommended adding a compact Merkle fingerprint to the append-only log to detect divergent states during reconciliation.
2026-01-28 - Marcus Nguyen: Added merkle checksum to log entries and a deterministic batch-commit algorithm. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1867
2026-01-30 - Data Eng (notes): Billing integration required a mapping from speculative charges to provisional invoices—raised ticket PM-489 for product discussion.

2026-02-02 - Load test results: 10k simulated tenants, 60s blackout per region. Speculative admit prevented 92% of 503s but increased reconciliation work by ~4.2% on controller post-recovery. Attached harness: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/blackout/sim-ephemeral-20260202

2026-02-03 - Asha Patel: Preparing canary plan and runbook; sequencing with release-ops for runtime-1.21. Noted need for a reversible feature-flag path and alerting on reconciliation_rejections > 0.5%.
